title: Measles vulnerability grows as vaccine rates slip in Washington - Axios
snippet: # Most Washington counties fall short of measles herd immunity. A measles outbreak this week in Snohomish County underscores broader vulnerability across Washington state, where vaccination coverage remains below protective levels. **Why it matters:** Measles spreads more easily when vaccination rates fall below 95% — a herd immunity threshold only four of Washington's 39 counties met among kindergartners this past school year, according to state data. **By the numbers:** Just 92.4% of King County kindergartners were vaccinated against measles in the 2024–25 school year, down from 95.6% in 2019–20. **The latest:** The three new measles cases confirmed in Snohomish County this week were among children who weren't vaccinated against the disease, county health officials said. * "Measles is a serious disease that often brings unpleasant symptoms, and in rare cases swelling of the brain and even death," Kim Van Pelt, Snohomish County's health department director, said in a written statement.

title: U.S. measles cases soar to 35-year high in 2026, already surpassing all of 2025 - NBC New York
snippet: # U.S. measles cases soar to 35-year high in 2026, already surpassing all of 2025. ## Experts say the spread might be greater than what’s known because the virus is one of the most contagious known to medicine and vaccination rates nationwide have declined. The number of measles cases in the U.S. has surpassed the record-breaking tally for all of 2025, with five more months of 2026 still to come. The nation had 2,289 cases in 2025, the worst year for measles in more than three decades. Furthermore, experts say the spread might be greater than what’s known because the virus is one of the most contagious known to medicine and vaccination rates nationwide have declined. In Utah, where public health officials have fought measles for more than a year, the virus has sickened more than 700 people during that time, according to the state health department.

title: Measles is back and more dangerous than most people realize. Here’s why doctors are worried - OregonLive.com
snippet: # Measles is back and more dangerous than most people realize. Measles is one of the world’s most contagious viruses, and that’s what makes even a small drop in vaccination rates so dangerous, doctors say. People can spread measles days before the telltale rash appears, when symptoms may look like a common cold, said Dr. Lorne Walker, a pediatric infectious disease specialist at Oregon Health & Science University. While many people recover, Walker said measles can cause serious complications, including pneumonia – the most common cause of measles-related death – and brain swelling that can cause permanent damage. That leaves people who get sick with measles more vulnerable to other infections for months or even years after they recover. The virus also can cause subacute sclerosing panencephalitis – a rare but fatal brain disorder that typically occurs seven to 10 years after a person has recovered from a measles infection. “There are people in our communities who are at higher risk, and we may not even realize it,” Walker said.
